en.name: Fried tofu puffs
en.summary: Fried tofu puffs keep 5–7 days refrigerated and 2–3 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). The Japanese manufacturing guidance for thick fried tofu, the closest documented product, gives roughly one week at 10 °C or below and stresses chilling immediately after frying, because the inside is still plain tofu.
en.pantry: Not a room-temperature food. The frying puffs the outside into a golden skin, but what is inside that skin is ordinary tofu — moist, low-acid and highly perishable — and fresh soy products are listed among the foods that spoil most readily. They must be chilled straight after frying and kept chilled; anything left out is in the danger zone of 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) and follows the two-hour rule, one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F). Buy them from a chilled counter rather than an unrefrigerated tray.
en.fridge: 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a sealed box, or to the printed date if it comes sooner. Keep them dry — puffs sitting in liquid go soggy and sour faster, and the whole point of the puff is that it is hollow and absorbent. If you have already simmered them in a braise or a hot pot, they are a cooked dish and follow the shorter timeline for leftovers rather than this one.
en.freezer: 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in a bag with the air pressed out. They freeze well: being mostly air, there is little water inside to form damaging ice crystals, and they go straight from the freezer into a soup or a braise. The window is set by the fried skin going rancid rather than by microbial spoilage — kept continuously frozen they stay safe well beyond it, and the smell of the oil is the thing to judge by.
en.thawing: No thawing needed — drop them straight into a simmering broth or hot pot from frozen. If you do thaw them, use the fridge and never the counter. Puffs thawed in the fridge and still cold may be refrozen with some quality loss.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened.
A stale, crayon-like smell from the fried skin — rancid oil.
Any mould spot, in which case the whole pack goes out.
tips: Keep them dry in a sealed box; sitting in liquid shortens their life.
Pour boiling water over them before cooking to strip excess surface oil.
Add them near the end of a simmer so they stay puffy rather than collapsing.
Freeze them in a bag with the air pressed out and cook straight from frozen.

faq.q: How long do fried tofu puffs keep?
faq.a: 5–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or to the printed date if sooner. Frozen, 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and they freeze unusually well because they are mostly air. Cook them straight from frozen.

faq.q: Are fried tofu puffs shelf-stable because they are fried?
faq.a: No. The frying only makes the skin; inside it is plain tofu, which is why they must be refrigerated promptly and treated as a fresh product.

zh.name: 油豆腐
zh.summary: 油豆腐冷藏可放 5～7 天，−18 °C 冷凍是 2～3 個月。日本針對厚炸豆腐（最接近、也有文件可循的產品）的製造指引，給的是 10 °C 以下約一週，並強調炸好要立刻冷藏，因為裡面仍然是普通豆腐。
zh.pantry: 這不是常溫食品。油炸把外層炸成金黃的皮，但皮裡面就是普通豆腐——含水量高、低酸、極易腐敗——而新鮮黃豆製品本來就被列為最容易壞的食物之一。它必須炸好就冷藏、全程冷藏；擺在外面的就在 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶裡，適用兩小時原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時只有一小時。請在冷藏櫃買，不要買常溫攤上的。
zh.fridge: 裝密封盒放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天；若印製日期更早，以日期為準。請保持乾爽——泡在水裡的油豆腐會更快變軟發酸，而油豆腐的全部意義就在於它是中空、會吸湯汁的。如果已經滷過或煮過火鍋，那它就是一道熟食，適用的是更短的剩菜期限，而不是這一條。
zh.freezer: 壓出空氣裝袋，−18 °C 下 2～3 個月。它很耐凍：裡面大半是空氣，沒有多少水可以結成破壞結構的冰晶，而且可以從冷凍直接丟進湯裡或滷鍋。決定這段期間的是炸皮油耗而不是微生物腐敗——只要全程沒退冰，超過它仍然安全，請以油的氣味為準。
zh.thawing: 不必解凍——直接從冷凍丟進滾著的湯或火鍋。真的要解凍就放冷藏，絕對不要放檯面。在冷藏解凍、還是冰的可以再冷凍，只是品質打折。
spoilage: 打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味。
炸皮聞起來陳、有蠟筆味——那是油耗。
出現任何霉點，整包丟掉。
tips: 裝密封盒、保持乾爽；泡在水裡會縮短它的壽命。
下鍋前用滾水淋過，沖掉多餘的表面油。
快起鍋前才下，才會保持蓬鬆而不是塌掉。
壓出空氣裝袋冷凍，要煮時直接從冷凍下鍋。

faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 5～7 天，或以更早的印製日期為準。冷凍則是 −18 °C 下 2～3 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 2～3 個月，而且非常耐凍，因為它裡面大半是空氣。直接從冷凍下鍋煮就好。

faq.q: 炸過的油豆腐可以放常溫嗎？
faq.a: 不行。油炸只做出外面那層皮，裡面還是普通豆腐；所以它必須盡快冷藏，並當成新鮮食品看待。
